bib.title: Talk Before You Retrieve: Agent-Led Discussions for Better RAG in Medical QA

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Talk Before You Retrieve: Agent-Led Discussions for Better RAG in Medical QA" (Discuss-RAG). Xuanzhao Dong (first author, equal contribution with Wenhui Zhu, Hao Wang, Xiwen Chen), Peijie Qiu, Rui Yin, Yi Su, Yalin Wang. Arizona State, Clemson, WashU, Banner Alzheimer's Institute. arXiv:2504.21252v1 [cs.CL], 30 Apr 2025. Preprint (no venue stated). Code: github.com/LLM-VLM-GSL/Discuss-RAG.

COVERAGE: 25622 of 25622 chars read, all 6 pages (references skimmed for origins). Figures were not rendered; I read only the extracted text of the captions and figure contents.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Adding Discuss-RAG to MedRAG raises answer accuracy on all four medical QA benchmarks.
   number: MMLU-Med 71.53 to 77.23 (+5.70); MedQA-US 62.45 to 66.85 (+4.40); BioASQ 58.61 to 75.28 (+16.67); PubMedQA 35.60 to 47.80 (+12.20). These are absolute percentage points.
   setup: MedRAG baseline with the textbook corpus (Jin et al., 2021) and the MedCPT retriever. LLM is gpt-3.5-turbo-0125. Metric is answer accuracy. The paper reports one number per cell, with no seeds, variance, or significance test. It does not say how many documents k were retrieved in the main run.
   quote: "BioASQ 58.61% 75.28% +16.67%" and "PubMedQA 35.60% 47.80% +12.20%"
   where: p.5, Table 1
2. Retrieval by dense similarity alone returns text that is topically related but not useful for the task. Even factually correct snippets can mislead the model.
   number: none
   setup: Preliminary qualitative study on MMLU-Med with GPT-3.5, textbook corpus fixed. Accuracy fluctuates across six subjects as k varies (Fig 2A). Three hand-picked questions are shown as examples. This is anecdotal, not a measured rate.
   quote: "snippets selected based solely on dense vector similarity with the query often retrieve content that is conceptually related but task-irrelevant."
   where: p.3, Sec 2
3. A single domain-expert agent that states the knowledge needed to answer, used together with the original query to guide retrieval, gave more relevant and better-organised snippets. The LLM then answered the example correctly (autosomal recessive question, Q3).
   number: none (one example)
   setup: A "medical geneticist" agent on one MMLU-Med question.
   quote: "When we used the agent's response, in conjunction with the original query, to guide retrieval, the resulting snippets were both more topically relevant and better organized."
   where: p.3, Sec 2
4. Method, step 1 (pre-retrieval). A recruiter agent assembles a team of expert agents. Each gives per-turn insights, and a summarizer folds them into a running summary. A verifier then checks the final summary for consistency and sufficiency and distils it. The distilled summary D is used for retrieval together with the original query Q. The agents are told not to answer the question.
   number: none. The example team has 3 agents.
   setup: Termination is a maximum of m rounds, or all agents declining to contribute. The paper does not give m.
   quote: "all agents in this module are explicitly instructed not to answer the original query or infer a final conclusion."
   where: p.4, Sec 3, Eq. 1: T^j := f_C(I_1^j,...,I_n^j; T^{j-1}, Q)
5. Method, step 2 (post-retrieval). A decision-maker agent U sees the distilled summary D, the query Q and the top-k chunks. If it rejects them, a fallback runs (a CoT prompt in their implementation). If it accepts, the chunks go into the context for answer generation.
   number: none
   quote: "If U returns a negative judgment, an alternative retrieval strategy is triggered (e.g., a CoT-based prompt (Wei et al., 2022) is used as a fallback in our implementation)."
   where: p.5, Sec 3
6. Both modules are plug-and-play for any training-free RAG pipeline.
   number: none
   quote: "both components of our proposed pipeline are designed as plug-and-play enhancements for any training-free RAG system."
   where: p.5

LIMITS
- No ablation. The gain is never split between the pre-retrieval discussion and the post-retrieval verifier, so the paper does not show which half matters.
- No cost, latency or token counts, and no number of agents or rounds.
- No retriever or LLM sweep: only GPT-3.5, MedCPT and one textbook corpus. Only the MedRAG baseline is compared. There are no other query-rewrite, HyDE or CRAG baselines.
- The "snippet quality" claim in the abstract and conclusion has no metric behind it. The evidence is Fig 4 only.
- PubMedQA baseline of 35.6% is low, so the large relative gain is on a weak baseline.
- Authors concede: (1) the expert agents do not talk to each other directly, only through the previous summary; (2) "Increased computational overhead" and engineering cost from prompting several LLM agents.
- The paper is a short 4-page style note. The prompts are not in the text, so they are in the repo, not the paper.

BUILDS ON: MedRAG (Xiong et al., 2024, Findings of ACL); MedCPT (Jin et al., 2023, Bioinformatics); chain-of-thought (Wei et al., 2022, NeurIPS); chain-of-verification RAG (He et al., 2024, arXiv:2410.05801); "Seven failure points" (Barnett et al., 2024, CAIN); MDAgents (Kim et al., 2024, NeurIPS); RETRO (Borgeaud et al., 2022); REALM (Guu et al., 2020); FiD (Izacard and Grave, 2020). Datasets: MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2020), MedQA (Jin et al., 2021), BioASQ (Tsatsaronis et al., 2015), PubMedQA (Jin et al., 2019).

CODE: none. The paper has only Eq. 1 and the pipeline diagram.

FIGURES (read from extracted text only)
- Fig 3 (p.4): "Illustration of the Discuss-RAG pipeline. (A) multi-turn brainstorming and summarization. (B) agent-led post-retrieval verification." This is the clearest single picture of recruiter, experts, summarizer, verifier, retriever, decision-maker, then fallback.
- Fig 2 (p.2): preliminary MMLU-Med study. (A) accuracy against k, (B) noisy and misleading snippet examples, (C) agent-led snippet selection. It shows the failure modes: noisy, misleading and over-generalised snippets.
- Fig 4 (p.4): MedQA-US example, MedRAG against Discuss-RAG. Fig 1 (p.1): RAG against a human's recall for an ibuprofen and gastric-ulcer question.

TARGET-NOTE FIT
- 08-agentic-rag-prince.md, strongest fit is "Clarify intent before retrieval" (line 54), which is only a gate (ask when the query is vague or the match is weak). Discuss-RAG goes further: it enriches the query with expert-derived background before retrieval and then checks the retrieved chunks. A secondary fit is "When agentic RAG pays" (line 690), because the paper's own limit is extra multi-agent cost. The note already says the field survey finds "corrective and hierarchical designs pay in latency" (line 700).
- A second fit is 11-retrieval-improvements.md, items 2 (multi-query) and 3 (HyDE), which cover query expansion before retrieval. Item 3 (line 245) covers "agent reasoning as free expansion" via AgentIR, and "What the paper's CRAG is" (line 48) covers the post-retrieval evaluator. Discuss-RAG is a multi-agent, LLM-prompted version of both halves: pre-retrieval expansion and post-retrieval gating.
- Grep result: no existing mention of Dong, Discuss-RAG, "Talk Before You Retrieve" or 2504.21252 in the notes or ../references.md. The idea of query expansion and a post-retrieval check is already present, but this paper's specific claim, an LLM expert panel that writes background before retrieval, is not. Given the weak evidence (one model, no ablation), this is a "sharpens" or a one-line mention with caveats, not a headline.
